subject: Aligning deep dive availability & performance goals
messages:
From: Avery Johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.com>
To: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@finova.com>, Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@finova.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning deep dive availability & performance goals

Hi Sam / Emily —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier today — really appreciated the level of detail you shared about the classification feature and where latency/cost are starting to become constraints. Quick recap and a suggested next step so we're aligned: 

Recap (from our discovery)
- Primary use: document classification + short-form summarization for customer support triage.
- Current traffic shape: spiky batch arrivals during EMEA mornings, sustained baseline in US PST business hours.
- Must-haves: 95th percentile generation latency under 500–700 ms for small prompts; predictable cost for nightly batch processing.
- Data controls: no PII stored on third-party; audit logs and regional routing required.

Proposed next step
We recommend a dedicated-capacity sizing deep dive to:
1) quantify throughput targets (QPS / concurrent requests) and typical prompt length distributions,
2) model batch vs. interactive profiles for cost/latency tradeoffs, and
3) map to a recommended dedicated pool configuration and autoscale policy.

Availability — proposed windows (all PT):
- Tue 25 May — 10:00–11:30 (60–90 min deep dive)
- Wed 26 May — 13:00–14:30 (alternate)

Attachments: redwood_intake_template.xlsx (short worksheet to capture sample traffic, token lengths, and SLOs). If you can fill the shaded rows before the call it will let us prepare rough sizing numbers in advance.

If either window works, I’ll send a calendar invite and include Monica (solutions engineer) and Ben (sales). Also, could you confirm an initial throughput goal (peak QPS or concurrent requests) and an example 95th latency target?

Thanks — looking forward to lining up the right folks.

Best,
Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.com

---
Attachment: redwood_intake_template.xlsx (worksheet)
From: Sam Rivera <sam.rivera@finova.com>

Cc: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@finova.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aligning deep dive availability & performance goals

Avery — thanks for the clear recap and the template. Both windows look plausible for us; Emily and I prefer Tue 25 May 10:00 PT if you can hold that.

Preliminary answers to your ask (we'll validate before the call):
- Peak concurrent requests: ~180–250 for real-time classification during surge periods (we'll send hourly breakdown).
- Average prompt size: ~180 tokens; 95th percentile prompt size ~420 tokens.
- Desired 95th percentile latency: target < 600 ms for the interactive path; nightly batch can be relaxed.
- Batch jobs: two nightly jobs that run in parallel with ~5000 items each; latency not critical but throughput matters for cost.

We attached a short workload summary that includes our traffic heatmap and a sample payload.

Quick Qs:
1) Do you want a test dataset ahead of time or is the intake sheet sufficient to start?
2) Will the sizing deep dive cover both routing (region failover) and KV-cache strategies for multi-turn?

Thanks — Sam
Sam Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering, Finova
sam.rivera@finova.com
